# Blue design rollout

Status: Authorized, in progress
Date: 2026-10-14 (Asia/Tbilisi)

The user selected the blue marketplace concept and authorized implementation and testing through the existing Claude agents. Codex coordinates and independently verifies. All four Angular UI apps are in scope. The backend and TestAPI are not changed. Preserve the user's pre-existing working changes. No commits, pushes, deployment, real purchases, or real redemption.

## Reference and concrete design contract

Selected concept: `C:/Users/georg/.codex/visualizations/2026/10/14/01a13bcf-2fba-74c1-946c-471991a11d75/service-token-directions.html`, first variant, blue clear marketplace. This is a direction reference, with illustrative data, not a complete pixel reference for all four apps. Keep real product information, functionality, current UI language and existing Angular bindings.

- Primary #2563EB, hover #1D4ED8, primary subtle #EAF1FF.
- Text #172033, secondary #596779, page #F4F7FB, surfaces #FFFFFF, borders #E0E6EE.
- Success #166534 (QA-corrected from #15803D to meet AA on #E7F5EC), danger #B91C1C, warning #92400E. Status labels accompany colors. Success green is semantic, not the primary brand.
- One shared visual language across all apps, replacing the cyan/green/violet/pink brand variants and unnecessary gradients with blue and neutral surfaces.
- 4/8px spacing rhythm. Page max width 1120px; desktop page gutters 24px, mobile 16px. Form/field spacing 12–16px, panels 20–24px desktop / 16px mobile. Cards 12px radius, large panels 16px, controls 8px. Subtle border and restrained shadow.
- Consistent existing Inter/system sans-serif stack. Body 14–16px, secondary >=12px, headings clear, aligned price numbers. No new remote assets needed.
- QA-corrected common focus ring: `0 0 0 2px #FFFFFF, 0 0 0 4px #2563EB` so button keyboard focus remains clear on light surfaces. Inputs keep their blue focus border. All four apps should use the same corrected shared token values.
- Primary controls have >=44px effective touch height, visible keyboard focus, readable disabled/hover/loading states. Solid blue buttons with white text. Neutral bordered secondary controls. Links must be readable on their actual surface.
- InvestorUI: bright service marketplace, clear cards with company/product/price/uses/validity, orderly filters, coherent cart/detail/checkout/payment-return/QR modal and auth/landing screens. Do not invent trading charts or fictitious product data.
- CompanyUI: calm requests/products/users tables, useful action hierarchy, responsive forms/dialogs, blue auth/landing/scanner treatment.
- AdminUI: dense neutral management surfaces, clear company/request tables and approval controls, blue auth treatment.
- ServiceUI: mobile-first scanning workflow, prominent camera/scanner action, clear scanning/processing/error/success outcomes, blue auth/landing. Source audit confirms the actual flow automatically redeems after reading a valid QR; preserve it and remove stale unreachable manual-confirm markup (see coordinator-findings.md). Any displayed QR uses a white background and dark modules for reliable reading. Do not change camera or redemption API contracts.

## Verification and pixel precision

Inspect each route and modal at 360x800, 768x1024, 1440x1000. No viewport overflow (tables may scroll within an explicitly contained wrapper), no overlaps, clipped labels/buttons or inaccessible dialogs. Check loading, empty, error, success, validation, disabled, focus, populated data. Review screenshot evidence against this spacing/color contract and the selected reference; do not claim a complete Figma-equivalent pixel match without a complete reference.

Both development and production builds must pass in each app. Claude QA writes/runs repeatable isolated local browser tests using bundled Playwright and headless Chrome with synthetic API fixtures; no production mutations. Test route navigation, modal open/close, filters, cart/checkout presentation, scanner states and forms. Do not add a dependency/test runner unnecessarily. Record exact findings/repro steps. Frontend agents fix design/regression findings, QA reruns until no reproducible bugs remain in the tested scope. Existing backend/security issues outside the redesign are recorded separately, not silently changed.

## Context policy

Each agent is a separate Claude CLI session, launched as its existing named role and configured model. The coordinator calibrates context capacity from CLI modelUsage.contextWindow, tracks per-message input+cache+output tokens (active context, not cumulative billing), and terminates the session at >=80%. 3	## InvestorUI: price hierarchy missing (design-contract gap)
4	
5	The frontend implementation report acknowledges that marketplace cards and detail surfaces do not show price. The selected blue concept and approved brief explicitly include a clear actual price.
6	
7	Frontend-engineer must render the real DTO price on primary/secondary market cards, the applicable detail modal and token detail page, with the blue concept's prominent neutral/tabular typography. Use the current app's currency convention; do not invent prices or change payment currency/logic. Correctly display a genuine zero rather than hiding it with a truthiness condition. 8	
9	Independent screenshot review (`investor_marketplace-primary_1440_populated.png`) also shows excessively stretched vertical spacing inside card metadata, and outlined add-to-cart actions where the selected concept uses a solid blue primary action. While integrating the price, make metadata follow a compact consistent gap/rhythm instead of flex-line stretching (inspect `token-card__body` flex-wrap/align-content); keep footers aligned without inserting large gaps between labels/values. Make the available market card's actual add-to-cart primary control solid #2563EB with white text; secondary management actions can remain neutral. Preserve real images, data, full readable titles and existing disabled/in-cart behavior. Verify this refinement in 360 and 1440 screenshots.
10	
11	## CompanyUI and InvestorUI: custom dialog keyboard/focus/scroll gaps
12	
13	Company's report explicitly says custom dashboard and scanner dialogs do not move focus or lock background scrolling. Investor's report leaves QR Escape/focus-return behavior unverified and only adds Escape for marketplace details. The designer's dialog rules require focus entry, keyboard containment, Escape/backdrop handling (unless submitting), focus return and background scroll locking. Verify and fix existing custom dialogs in all apps as needed, using a shared helper where it avoids duplicated logic. Avoid changing business submission/camera/SignalR behavior. With nested Investor detail/QR dialogs, preserve the outer dialog's lock and focus when the inner dialog closes. Existing confirm-dialog logic may already cover these requirements: inspect before changing it.
14	
15	QA should explicitly verify focus moves inside on open, Tab/Shift+Tab stay within, Escape closes when allowed, focus returns to trigger, and body scrolling is restored after final close/unmount. Disabled/submitting behavior must remain correct.
16	
17	These are reproducible source-backed remaining items; do not mark the whole rollout complete while they remain open.
18	
19	## ServiceUI: verification and submitting state
20	
21	Service frontend report says production build emitted output but its shell exited 127. Treat this as unverified until an independent direct build exits 0. The report also acknowledges missing focus entry on scanner open, and Escape/backdrop cancellation while a redemption request is submitting. Apply the common dialog requirements above. During submitting, prevent user dismissal (Escape/backdrop/close/cancel) consistently until the existing request resolves, keeping success/error cleanup and camera teardown intact. QA must use a delayed synthetic redemption fixture to test this, and verify camera-denied/error/retry presentation without accessing real hardware.
22	
23	### Important scanner source clarification (CompanyUI and ServiceUI)
24	
25	Independent source inspection shows the current **real** QR flow automatically calls `POST /ServiceToken/GetService` after validating the detected payload. It does not GET details or enter a manual confirm state. Existing comments, CLAUDE descriptions and the copied confirmation template are stale: `confirm()` is referenced in the template but no such component method exists; `token` is never populated, and that branch is unreachable. **Preserve the existing automatic redemption behavior; do not add a new manual confirmation workflow or invent a read endpoint.**
26	
27	Adapt the redesigned state presentation to the actual flow: scanning -> visible submitting/processing -> existing success/error outcome. Use submitting for the in-flight POST so close/Escape/backdrop guards protect the actual pending operation, not only an unreachable state. Remove the dead confirmation branch/undefined template handler and obsolete display-only state/helpers as appropriate; keep camera-denied/invalid-QR retry states. Guard duplicate decode callbacks before awaiting scanner stop so a QR read cannot issue duplicate POSTs. Preserve API params, QR payload and notifications. QA must test the actual handler and assert exactly one mocked POST plus delayed-request dismissal guard; do not mark synthetic manually-forced unreachable confirmation screenshots as runtime coverage.
28	
29	Validate parsed QR as unknown before accessing fields: JSON `null`, arrays/primitives, missing fields or wrong field types must show the existing invalid/missing QR feedback, issue no POST and support rescan. The old `JSON.parse(text) as QrPayload` followed by `.tokenId` can throw for valid JSON null; this is a concrete error-state defect. Preserve zero rowVersion as valid when properly typed; use finite integer/nonnegative validation matching the existing uint contract. Keep asynchronous camera cleanup reliable if the component is destroyed while camera startup is pending.
30	
31	Current C# `ServiceTokenDto` has RemainingCount, ServiceCount, Price and statuses None=0, Available=1, Sold=2, InCart=3, Finished=255. Company/Service copied DTO models still use count/old status values, but their live automatic scanner response is void and never renders that DTO. Do not invent displayed token details from these stale models. If any **reachable** UI actually consumes these values, synchronize only the affected UI consumers to the existing backend contract, without backend edits; otherwise record the unused stale model separately.
32	
33	## AdminUI: independently verified QA defects
34	
35	Read its first QA report for precise reproduction. Fix the real status text contrast failure; make desktop request-table actions reliably reachable (e.g. restrained wrapping for wide dates/columns or sticky action column without viewport overflow); restore focus to the opener on confirm dialog close. Keep the explicitly permitted mobile table scrolling.
36	
37	## Shared UI details: focus and visible error feedback
38	
39	Strengthen button-only focus indicators so they have a clearly visible, sufficiently contrasted blue outline/ring against white/light surfaces (the .35-alpha shadow on its own is too faint, about 1.7:1). Verify keyboard focus after CSS transitions settle. Do not remove the valid blue border/ring on inputs or change the primary palette.
40	
41	Admin QA observed an empty/undefined toast message when a synthetic 500 response has an empty body. Even though pre-existing, this is an error-presentation defect within the approved loading/empty/error state contract. In the redesigned shared toast handling, ensure an error always gets an existing or concise English generic fallback if no usable message exists; never expose raw credentials/stack/data. Apply the same defensive presentation rule where needed in each app. Preserve retry actions and API behavior. QA must check empty-body 500/network-error messages are readable and nonempty.
42
